title: Bounded Confluence Theorem

basis.scope: Canonical bounded confluence semantics for continuation classes that already satisfy well-formedness, typing, local confluence, determinism, termination, and uniqueness prerequisites.

core_rule.statement: Bounded confluence applies only to admissible bounded continuation classes satisfying WF(C), Typed(C), C ⇓L, Det(C), Term(C), and Unique(C); every lawful reduction branch from such a class terminates and the terminating branches are process-equivalent modulo ≡P; RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Establish the first bounded confluence theorem for the RT Calculus. The theorem applies only to continuation classes satisfying the previously established local confluence, determinism, termination, and uniqueness conditions. No claim of universal confluence is made.

canonical_claims.statement: Bounded confluence applies only to continuation classes satisfying the established prerequisite bundle.
Every lawful reduction branch from an admissible bounded continuation class terminates.
All terminating branches are process-equivalent modulo ≡P.
Bounded confluence does not imply global confluence or Church-Rosser.

formal_objects.name: Bounded Confluence
formal_objects.definition: The property that all lawful reduction branches belonging to an admissible bounded continuation class converge to process-equivalent canonical outcomes.

formal_objects.name: Confluence Class
formal_objects.definition: A continuation class satisfying all bounded confluence prerequisites.

then: Every lawful reduction branch from C terminates.
All terminating branches are process-equivalent modulo ≡P.
Representative canonical forms belong to the same equivalence class [NF(C)]≡P.

proof_obligations.description: All reduction steps satisfy typed transition rules.
Every critical reduction pair is joinable.

bounded_results.result: Equivalent reduction branches preserve process equivalence.

limitations: Applies only to bounded continuation classes.
Does not establish universal reduction uniqueness outside bounded classes.
invariants: Trace identity is independent of confluence.
Equivalent reduction outcomes remain classified as NF(C), pNF(C), or ⊥C_x.
